threat_actors.name: DeepSeek

attack_patterns.name: Extract AI Model
attack_patterns.description: Chinese firms used a technique called 'knowledge distillation' to query U.S. models (including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok) billions of times to train their own 'student' models, effectively replicating the capabilities of the 'teacher' models.

attack_patterns.name: Establish Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The Chinese firms created numerous accounts on U.S. AI platforms, likely using automated scripts, to bypass basic rate limiting and account creation controls for their distillation campaigns.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors utilized distributed infrastructure to carry out the large-scale querying attacks and evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Proxy
attack_patterns.description: The firms employed techniques to mask their activity, such as using residential proxies to evade detection and fingerprinting while querying U.S. AI models.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The large-scale querying campaigns resulted in high computational costs for the U.S. providers, constituting a form of economic denial of service and abuse of the providers' computational resources.

attack_patterns.name: AI Model Inference API Access
attack_patterns.description: The attack was conducted by abusing legitimate API access to the target AI models (GPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok) at a massive scale to perform knowledge distillation.

campaigns.name: Chinese AI Model Theft Campaigns
campaigns.description: A series of systematic, industrial-scale campaigns by China-based AI companies to illicitly extract capabilities from U.S.-developed foundational AI models using knowledge distillation. The campaigns began around late 2024.
campaigns.objective: Steal intellectual property from U.S. AI models to accelerate development of Chinese AI models.

identities.name: U.S. AI Companies
identities.description: A class of U.S.-based AI development companies whose foundational models (including GPT, Gemini, Claude, and Grok) were targeted for intellectual property theft via knowledge distillation.

identities.name: National Security Agency
identities.description: One of the U.S. security agencies that co-authored the joint advisory warning of Chinese AI model theft campaigns.

infrastructure.name: Querying and Evasion Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Distributed infrastructure, including residential proxies and numerous automatically-created accounts, used to send billions of queries to U.S. AI models and evade detection.

indicators.name: Potential AI Model Knowledge Distillation Activity
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential AI Model Knowledge Distillation Activity
id: 7e5f8b1a-9c3d-4e2f-8a1b-6c4d5e3f2a1b
status: experimental
description: Detects a combination of behaviors that may indicate an AI model knowledge distillation campaign, including high request volumes from non-corporate user agents to common AI API endpoints.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/cisa-nsa-and-fbi-warn-china-based-ai-companies-targeting-us-ai-models-industrial-scale-knowledge
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-09
tags:
  - attack.aml.t0024.002
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_endpoint:
    c-uri-path|endswith: '/v1/chat/completions'
  selection_ua:
    c-user-agent|contains:
      - 'python-requests'
      - 'curl'
      - 'Wget'
      - 'Java/'
  filter_legit_sdk:
    c-user-agent|startswith:
      - 'OpenAI/v1'
      - 'anthropic-sdk-python'
      - 'google-api-python-client'
  condition: all of selection_* and not filter_legit_sdk
indicators.description: Detects behavioral patterns indicative of AI model knowledge distillation, such as high-volume API requests to chat completion endpoints from non-standard user agents, as described in the joint advisory.

indicators.name: Programmatic User Account Creation Pattern
indicators.pattern:
title: Programmatic User Account Creation Pattern
id: 8d2c1a0b-4e5f-4b9c-8a1d-7b6e5f4d3c2a
status: experimental
description: Detects user account creation using programmatic naming conventions (e.g., user12345), which may indicate automated account generation for AI service abuse.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/cisa-nsa-and-fbi-warn-china-based-ai-companies-targeting-us-ai-models-industrial-scale-knowledge
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-09
tags:
  - attack.t1585
  - attack.resource_development
level: medium
logsource:
  category: application
  product: generic
detection:
  selection:
    username|re: 'user[0-9]{4,}'
    event_type: 'account_creation'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects suspicious account creation patterns, such as programmatic usernames, which are used to generate the numerous accounts needed for large-scale distillation campaigns.
